pr_title: New util "data_size" (convert between SI and IEC data units) + filesize unit parameter
pr_body:
## Breaking change

This integration now uses common HA constants as configuration keys. That means that existing YAML configurations need to be adjusted or alternatively re-created using the new config flow (via the "Integrations" config menu in HA):

`file_paths` renamed to `file_path` (plural to singular)
`file_path` now also can only contain a single path to match what the newly config flow can handle, so lists need to be split up into separate configuration entries.

Existing entity IDs will also change (so you will need to adjust references e.g., in dashboards or automations) since they are now constructed as follows to ensure we can handle the same file name in different paths:
`sensor.<slugified file path>_<unit of measurement>`

Example: sensor.home_spacegaier_homeassistant_home_assistant_v2_db_gb for file "/home/spacegaier/.homeassistant/home-assistant_v2.db" in GB.

## Proposed change
In order to allow the user to specify the output unit of measure e.g. for the `filesize` integration, we need to convert between data size units. This PR adds such a HA util, that can handle both SI and IEC units.

It also add a new optional parameter for `filesize` to specify the desired unit of measurement. "MB" is still used as default.

The PR also introduces a config flow which is the reason for the breaking config structure changes.

## Type of change
<!--
  What type of change does your PR introduce to Home Assistant?
  NOTE: Please, check only 1! box! 
  If your PR requires multiple boxes to be checked, you'll most likely need to
  split it into multiple PRs. This makes things easier and faster to code review.
-->

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New integration (thank you!)
- [X] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Example entry for `configuration.yaml`:
<!--
  Supplying a configuration snippet, makes it easier for a maintainer to test
  your PR. Furthermore, for new integrations, it gives an impression of how
  the configuration would look like.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR does not have an example entry.
-->

```yaml
# Example configuration.yaml
  - platform: filesize
    file_path: /home/philip/.homeassistant/home-assistant_v2.db
  - platform: filesize
    file_path: /home/philip/.homeassistant/home-assistant_v2.db
    unit_of_measurement: "MiB"  
  - platform: filesize
    file_path: /home/philip/.homeassistant/home-assistant_v2.db
    unit_of_measurement: "GB"
  - platform: filesize
    file_path: /home/philip/.homeassistant/home-assistant_v2.db
    unit_of_measurement: "B"
  - platform: filesize
    file_path: /home/philip/.homeassistant/home-assistant_v2.db
    unit_of_measurement: "KiB"
  - platform: filesize
    file_path: /home/philip/.homeassistant/home-assistant_v2.db
    unit_of_measurement: "kB"
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/114137/84566525-1fd2b100-ad72-11ea-8cea-e7bb7b119e8e.png)

## The problem

  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.

File size in MB is wrongly calculated. See attached screenshot where **bytes** and **MB** are the same value.

Correct formula should be "total bytes / 1024 / 1024".

  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.111.0
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Docker
- Integration causing this issue: filesize
- Link to integration documentation on our website:

<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even

  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->


<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>
Depends on who you ask I would say; If one follows the internal system of units (SI), the current is actually correct. Furthermore, your given calculation refers to the binary prefix, which is expressed as MiB, not MB.

Good point, even if most system still use 2^20 for files size and instead use 10^6 for network related calculations.

I ca easily solve using a custom sensor, but I think "MiB" should be added as attribute so nobody would have any doughs in future ;-)

Simone
I am working on adding that support. I already implemented a new `data_size` HA util that can convert between any SI and IEC data unit and added an optional parameter to the configuration for the user to set for the `filesize` integration. More details in the PR I am going to create soon.
